report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. High-quality clinical trial evidence confirms that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix) significantly reduces the risk of developing shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged 70 years or older.

**Evidence Summary:**
- **High Vaccine Efficacy:** The pivotal Phase 3 randomized controlled trial (ZOE-70) evaluated the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine in nearly 14,000 adults aged 70 years and older. The study found a vaccine efficacy of approximately 90% against shingles in this population, with high protection maintained across both the 70–79 and ≥80 age brackets.
- **Reduction in Complications:** Pooled analyses from the ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 clinical trials confirmed that vaccine efficacy against shingles remained greater than 90% in adults aged 70 or older. The vaccine also substantially reduced the incidence of postherpetic neuralgia, the most common debilitating complication of shingles.
- **Sustained Immune Response:** Unlike older live-attenuated vaccines (e.g., Zostavax), whose efficacy dropped significantly in adults over 70, the addition of an adjuvant in the recombinant vaccine triggers a strong, durable immune response even in older individuals experiencing immunosenescence. This led health agencies like the U.S. CDC to recommend the adjuvanted recombinant vaccine for adults 50 and older.

**Sources Cited:**
- https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800
- https://shingrixhcp.com/efficacy-safety/efficacy-data/
- https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/hcp/vaccine-considerations/index.html
- https://academic.oup.com/rheumatology/article/60/3/1226/5903548
